myasthenia: Abnormal weakness of the muscles; but especially myasthenia gravis.
myasthenic: Of, pertaining to, or suffering from myasthenia.
mycelial: Of or pertaining to the mycelium
mycelian: Of or relating to the mycelium.
mycelium: The vegetative part of any fungus, consisting of a mass of branching, threadlike hyphae, often underground.
mycetoma: Chronic subcutaneous inflammation caused by infection with certain bacteria or fungi.
mycobacterium: Any of many rod-shaped, aerobic bacteria, of the genus Mycobacterium, that cause diseases such as tuberculosis and leprosy.
mycoflora: Fungi collectively, especially those of a particular region
mycological: Of or pertaining to mycology or to fungi
mycologically: In terms of, or by means of, mycology.
mycologist: A person who studies, professes or practices mycology.
mycophile: A person who likes hunting for, cooking or eating mushrooms and other edible fungi.
mycoplasma: Any infectious bacterium of the genus Mycoplasma, often specifically Mycoplasma pneumoniae
mycorrhiza: A plant root formed in symbiosis with a fungus; the symbiosis between the mycelium of a fungus and the roots of a plant.
mycorrhizal: Of or pertaining to a mycorrhiza.
mycosis: An infection caused by a fungus.
mycotic: Of or relating to a fungus.
mycotoxin: Any substance, produced by a mold or fungus, that is injurious to vertebrates upon ingestion, inhalation or skin contact.
mydriasis: The condition of having abnormally large and dilated pupils due to illness or narcotics, particularly stimulants such as methamphetamine, cocaine, etc.
mydriatic: Pertaining to or causing mydriasis (the dilation of the pupil of the eye).
myelencephalic: Alternative form of myelencephalous (“Of or pertaining to the myelencephalon; cerebrospinal”).
myelencephalon: The portion of the brain composed of the medulla oblongata.
myelin: A white, fatty material, composed of lipids and lipoproteins, that surrounds the axons of nerves.
myelinated: Of nerves, having a coating of myelin.
myelitis: Inflammation of the spinal cord or of bone marrow.
myeloblast: An immature cell of bone marrow that develops into a myelocyte.
myeloblastic: Of, pertaining to or containing myeloblasts.
myelocyte: A large cell, found in bone marrow, that becomes a granulocyte when mature.
myelofibrosis: collagen deposition by fibroblasts in the bone marrow, whether primary or secondary to other causes such as medication.
myelogenous: Originating in, or produced by, bone marrow
myeloid: Of or pertaining to bone marrow.
myeloma: A malignant tumour arising from cells of the bone marrow, specifically plasma cells.
myelopathy: A disorder in which the tissue of the spinal cord is diseased or damaged.
myeloproliferative: of or pertaining to the presence of an abnormal proliferation of myelopoietic cells (from bone marrow)
myiasis: The infestation of a living vertebrate by maggots.
mylonite: Any rock that has undergone modifications due to dynamic recrystallization following plastic flow; a schist created by crushed or ground rock.
myna: One of the South and East Asian birds of the starling family Sturnidae.
mynheer: Sir, as a polite form of address to a Dutchman or Afrikaner.
myoblast: An undifferentiated stem cell that develops into muscle tissue.
myocardial: Relating to the myocardium, the thick muscular wall of the heart.
myocardium: The muscular substance of the heart; the middle of the three layers forming the outer wall of the human heart.
myoclonic: Of or pertaining to myoclonus; consisting of or characterized by sudden jerking motions.
myoclonus: The brief, involuntary twitching of a muscle or group of muscles.
myofibril: Any of the cylindrical organelles, found within muscle cells, that are the contractile unit of muscles.
myofilament: A filament within a myofibril, constructed from proteins
myogenic: Forming muscle fibres; pertaining to myogenesis.
myoglobin: A small globular protein, containing a heme group, that carries oxygen to muscles.
myograph: An instrument for determining and recording the intensity, velocity, etc., of a muscular contraction.
myoinositol: The most commonly-occurring isomer of inositol.
myologic: Of or pertaining to the study of muscles or muscle tissue.
myoma: A tumor composed of muscle tissue, usually benign and commonly occurring in the uterus and the esophagus.
myomatous: Of or pertaining to a myoma.
myoneural: neuromuscular; relating to the muscles and nerves
myopathy: Any of several diseases of muscle that are not caused by nerve disorders
myopia: A disorder of the vision where distant objects appear blurred because the eye focuses their images in front of the retina instead of on it.
myopic: Near-sighted; unable to see distant objects unaided.
myoscope: An instrument for studying the muscles.
myosin: Any of a large family of motor proteins found in eukaryotic tissues, allowing mobility in muscles.
myosotis: Any plant of the genus Myosotis, the forget-me-nots.
myotome: In vertebrate embryonic development, a group of tissues formed from any particular one of the somites that develop into the body wall muscle.
myotonia: A symptom of several muscular disorders characterized by the slow relaxation of the muscles after voluntary contraction or electrical stimulation.
myriapod: Any arthropod (such as centipedes and millipedes) of the subphylum Myriapoda.
myrica: Any member of the genus Myrica of shrubs and trees.
myrmecophile: An organism, especially an insect, that lives in close association with or shares a nest with a species of ant.
myrmecophilous: Adapted to thrive in the presence of ants.
myrmidon: A soldier or a subordinate civil officer who executes orders of a superior without protest or pity (sometimes applied to bailiffs, constables, etc).
myrobalan: A plum-like fruit from various trees of the genus Terminalia, formerly used in medicine and now in the dyeing industry; also, the tree itself.
myrrh: A red-brown resinous material, the dried sap of a tree of the genus Commiphora, especially Commiphora myrrha, used as perfume, incense or medicine.
myrrhic: Of, related to, or derived from myrrh.
myrtle: An evergreen shrub or small tree of the genus Myrtus, native to southern Europe and north Africa.
myself: Me, as direct or indirect object the speaker as the object of a verb or preposition, when the speaker is also the subject.
mysid: Any crustacean of the order Mysida.
mystagogue: A person who prepares an initiate for entry into a mystery cult, or who teaches mystical doctrines.
mystagogy: The doctrines, principles, or practice of a mystagogue; interpretation of mysteries.
mystery: Something secret or unexplainable; an unknown.
mystic: Of, or relating to mystics, mysticism or occult mysteries; mystical.
mysticism: The beliefs, ideas, or thoughts of mystics.
mystification: The act of mystifying or the condition of being mystified.
mystified: simple past and past participle of mystify
mystifier: A person who obscures or muddles information, making something appear to be a mystery.
mystifies: third-person singular simple present indicative of mystify
mystify: To thoroughly confuse, befuddle, or bewilder.
mystique: An aura of heightened interest, meaning or mystery surrounding a person or thing.
myth: A traditional story which embodies a belief regarding some fact or phenomenon of experience, and in which often the forces of nature and of the soul are personified; a sacred na…
mythically: In relation to or by means of myth
mythicized: simple past and past participle of mythicize
mythicizes: third-person singular simple present indicative of mythicize
mythicizing: present participle and gerund of mythicize
mythier: comparative form of mythy: more mythy
mythiest: superlative form of mythy: most mythy
mythmaker: A person who originates a myth.
mythmaking: The production or composing of myths.
mythographer: one who studies or writes down myths and legends
mythography: A depiction of a myth in literature or the arts.
mythological: Of, or relating to myths or mythology.
mythologically: In a mythological fashion or manner.
mythologize: To interpret (a story etc.) as mythological; to explain the symbolic meaning of.
mythologized: simple past and past participle of mythologize.
mythologizes: third-person singular simple present indicative of mythologize
mythologizing: present participle and gerund of mythologize
mythology: The collection of myths of a people, concerning the origin of the people, history, deities, ancestors and heroes.
mythomania: A compulsion to tell lies and exaggerate the truth.
mythopoeic: Giving rise to myths; pertaining to the creation of myth.
mythopoetic: Giving rise to myths; pertaining to the creation of myth.
mythopoetical: Pertaining to the creation of myths; pertaining to mythopoiesis.
mythos: Anything transmitted by word of mouth, such as a fable, legend, narrative, story, or tale (especially a poetic tale).
mythy: Of or pertaining to myth; mythical.
myxedema: A form of cutaneous and dermal edema that is secondary to increased deposition of connective tissue components in subcutaneous tissue.
myxocyte: A certain polyhedral or stellate cell, found in mucous tissue.
myxoma: A tumor consisting of primitive connective tissue and mucous elements.
myxomatosis: A usually fatal viral disease of rabbits, causing skin tumors.
myxomycete: Any protozoan of the phylum Myxomycota; the slime molds.
myxovirus: Any of a group of RNA viruses of the Orthomyxoviridae and Paramyxoviridae families.
